findings.summary: The prior Final review's sole REJECT finding (rf-49b88ef6: request acceptance and call admission not atomic) is addressed. GoalRequestKernel now holds a per-kernel _request_lock (threading.RLock) that serializes the submit (dedup -> durable append -> enqueue -> mode wake), next_goal_call (resume/fence/mode -> pop -> claim -> call record), and abort_unavailable_call (release fence -> re-queue front) transitions; the guarded sections are in-memory + journal-mutating only. Offline barrier-controlled regressions pin concurrent duplicate submission, distinct-submission journal/queue order, and exactly-once claim without a dropped request.

Goal version activation remains unwired into the production composition path: build_line constructs GoalRequestKernel without calling activate_version, so active_version stays empty until a live version event arrives. The explicit-version and stale-version-refusal semantics are fully implemented and offline-tested (TestExplicitGoalVersions, TestStaleVersionApproval, TestLiveVersionAtReviewBoundary); wiring a goal.md content_revision -> activate_version source is deferred integration consistent with the spec's deferred later slices, not a development-stage violation.

input_commit, subject_commit, and implementation_subject_commit are all the identical full identity 33e3a68fcfd5259484f4858c8366c20b331f01b4. The product tree was inspected directly by file review; the mechanical product-tree-equivalence diff between work_head_commit 7e089eb35a880fc613b7fd1e9ff4a59e87135d2a and the materialization subject, and actual Git HEAD, remain the deterministic seal's responsibility (no shell or Git command was executed).
